### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via defaultRowScope (literal, a string literal in DEFAULT_ROW_SCOPE_KEY))_
- `content/docs/permissions/access-recipes.mdx`  _(via rowLevelSecurity (literal, a string literal in RLS_POLICIES_KEY))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permission-metadata.mdx`  _(via rowLevelSecurity (literal, a string literal in RLS_POLICIES_KEY))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`  _(via rowLevelSecurity (literal, a string literal in RLS_POLICIES_KEY))_
- `content/docs/permissions/rls.mdx`  _(via rowLevelSecurity (literal, a string literal in RLS_POLICIES_KEY))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx`  _(via rowLevelSecurity (literal, a string literal in RLS_POLICIES_KEY))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx`  _(via rowLevelSecurity (literal, a string literal in RLS_POLICIES_KEY))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via rowLevelSecurity (literal, a string literal in RLS_POLICIES_KEY))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via rowLevelSecurity (literal, a string literal in RLS_POLICIES_KEY))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via rowLevelSecurity (literal, a string literal in RLS_POLICIES_KEY))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via defaultRowScope (literal, a string literal in DEFAULT_ROW_SCOPE_KEY))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via rowLevelSecurity (literal, a string literal in RLS_POLICIES_KEY))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **246** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **181** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **181**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **122** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json de141e329575427273ae3a9a575fd8077199bd9c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b3f95dc7900336b16c390b9ba29a88fffff90e70` — the merge of head `2c3850332884384d6470d14cedab8991b53f9e48` into base `de141e329575427273ae3a9a575fd8077199bd9c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b3f95dc7900336b16c390b9ba29a88fffff90e70 && git checkout b3f95dc7900336b16c390b9ba29a88fffff90e70
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin de141e329575427273ae3a9a575fd8077199bd9c 2c3850332884384d6470d14cedab8991b53f9e48 && git checkout -B drift-repro de141e329575427273ae3a9a575fd8077199bd9c && git merge --no-ff 2c3850332884384d6470d14cedab8991b53f9e48

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json de141e329575427273ae3a9a575fd8077199bd9c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs de141e329575427273ae3a9a575fd8077199bd9c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c448e8e3eb196e5e66c8d5d80f46ad1e04977f85`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/inline-grid-columns.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-field-consumers.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts

Inputs read: card #32256 (body and all 5 comments: claim, amendments 1 and 2, triage, os-dev-report), PR #32276 (body, 9-file list, net diff against `main`), and the check-runs on the head. The PR has no comments and no earlier record.

Check-runs on the head, read at the end of the review (44 runs): 13 `success` (Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check PR Size, Auto Label, Flag docs affected by code changes, Plan Test Core shards, Plan Test UI shards, filter), 10 `skipped`, 0 failed, and 21 still `in_progress`: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, all four Type Check jobs (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI. In-progress runs are not green. The verdict below is the contract judgment only; the typecheck that proves the `satisfies` lines and the test shards had not concluded, and nothing here stands in for them.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface, `@objectstack/spec/data`: one new export, `deriveInlineGridSortField (function)`.** Right. `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` each gain exactly that line. `INLINE_GRID_SORT_FIELDS` is still reached by relative import only: no barrel line, no subpath, no baseline line. That is what claim amendment 2 ruled (option A).
- **What the export publishes.** The six names are not exported, but the derivation over them now is, so their membership and the first-in-field-order rule are public behaviour of this function from here on. That is the cost of option A as ruled, and it is the same position `deriveInlineGridColumns` already put the names in (it skips them). Right, as ruled.
- **Spec accept set: unchanged.** No schema, no `authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` shard moves. Right.
- **Lint verdict set: narrows only.** `field-no-consumers` (a warning) stops reporting three shapes: a field read by `permissions[].rowLevelSecurity[].using` / `.check`; a field read by `objects[].defaultRowScope.using` / `.check`; the derived line-position field of a child that some inline grid draws. No new finding can appear: every change adds a `behaviour` site and none removes or downgrades one. Right.
- **`CARRIER_ROOTS` unchanged** (`permissions` stays in it), so the `Roots scanned` line of the explanation and its test hold. Right.

### ② Semver level

- **Level: `patch` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/lint`. Right.** The gate's own rule (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, "The LEVEL axis", maintainer ruling A on #25105; AGENTS.md Post-Task 3): the level follows the metadata protocol alone, a `none` grades every entry `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. A new helper export changes nothing a metadata author can write, so `minor` would be refused, not preferred. The 2026-09-04 "additive widening takes at least minor" rule is the one ruling A amended.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`. Right.** No authorable key, value or type moves.
- **Clause-②: `no` is the wrong value. should-fix.** The line answers "does this PR widen a published accept set or public surface" (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`; the gate's own help text: `no` means "widens no published accept set or public surface"). This PR adds an export to a published entry point and moves its api-surface baseline, so the answer is `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. Precedent on `main`: 93ff5dde declared `yes (widening)` + `Metadata-protocol: none` + `patch` for "new exported contracts", and passed. The seat's claim amendment 2 pre-wrote `no` on the ground that no schema accept-set moves; that reads half of the question. Nothing downstream changes with the fix: the level stays `patch`, `added` is not declared so there is no contradiction, and the contract review is owed by the schema face either way. It is still a wrong declaration that ships in the changeset body. Fix: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` in the PR body and in `.changeset/32256-field-consumers-rls-and-grid-position.md`; the changeset edit moves the head and earns a delta review.
- `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on this head. It cannot see this: for a public-surface widening the declaration, not the diff, is the carrier.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation: `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts` edited beyond the claimed file surface.** Accepted. `os explain field-no-consumers` is the rule's long-form contract and would otherwise contradict the rule. Judged in ④.
- **Deviation: the `defaultRowScope` arm.** Accepted as in scope. Same file, same defect class (a row-policy predicate not read as an expression), same predicate function, pinned by a test and ablated. Correct against the schema: `DefaultRowScopeSchema` is the policy shape minus `object`, built from the same members, so `using` and `check` exist on it with the same meaning, and `plugin-security/src/object-default-row-scope.ts` reads it. The card's text names only `permissions`, so this is wider than the ask; it is the quiet direction and no object in the tree declares the key yet.
- **Deviation: rebase onto `d391babc` before first push; PR body header order; skipped harness steps.** No contract effect.
- **`open_questions`: empty.**
- **Out-of-scope note 1: a field permission's `when` stays a carrier.** Answered by the card ("leave every other path under `permissions` as a carrier") and true in the tree. It is the same false-positive class as this card, since the spec describes `when` as a CEL row condition on the edit vote, so it deserves a follow-up card rather than silence. Not owed here.
- **Out-of-scope note 2: `current_user.email` credits a same-named field on the policy's object.** True, and it is the scan every expression site already gets. Accepted; see the nit in ④.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/inline-grid-columns.ts` (hits).**

- Agrees with the renderer. `deriveDetail` in `ui/packages/plugin-form/src/deriveMasterDetail.ts` line 535 takes the first key of `childSchema.fields`, in `Object.keys` order, that `SORT_FIELD_NAMES` has, and its `SORT_FIELD_NAMES` (line 55) holds the same six names as the spec's private set. The helper is the same expression over the spec's set: first match in field-map order, no type or flag consulted, `undefined` on no match or no field map. `MasterDetailForm.tsx` takes `sortField` from that derivation on both the authored-columns branch (line 1368) and the derived branch (line 1385), hands it to the grid, and adds it to the child fetch's `$orderby` (line 1648). The jsdoc claims "every inline grid resolves it, authored columns or derived" and "stamps on drag-reorder and loads ordered by it"; both hold.
- Name and signature are sane. `(def: unknown): string | undefined` matches its siblings `deriveInlineGridColumns(def: unknown, …)` and `deriveInlineRowFormFields(def: unknown, …)`, uses the same `prop(def, 'fields')` guard, and the name matches the renderer's `sortField` and the private set's name.
- The private list stays private, as its header requires. No finding.
- nit: the renderer does not call this helper. `deriveMasterDetail.ts` keeps its own literal `SORT_FIELD_NAMES`, and nothing pins the two lists equal, so "the renderer's own rule, reproduced exactly" is true today by inspection only. The duplication predates this PR, but a lint credit now rests on it. Follow-up card: have the renderer import `deriveInlineGridSortField`, as it already imports `isInlineRowFormOffered`. `ui/**` is outside this claim.
- nit: `inline-grid-sort-fields.ts` (not in the diff) still describes `inline-grid-columns.ts` as the reader that skips the names; it now also picks from them. The sentence "Two readers here" stays true. Left as is.

**`packages/lint/src/validate-field-consumers.ts` (implementing).**

- RLS credit, sentence by sentence. `bucketFor` returns `behaviour` inside a carrier root only for `isRlsPredicateSite` or the pre-existing `externalId` / `upsertKey` segments; everything else under `permissions` is still `carrier`. `scanText` adds the bare-identifier shape only for `EXPRESSION_KEYS` or `isRlsPredicateSite`. The predicate test requires the last two segments to be exactly (`rowLevelSecurity`, `using`|`check`) under root `permissions`, or (`defaultRowScope`, `using`|`check`) under root `objects`. The policy's object is resolved by `contextOf` from the policy's own `object`, so the credit lands on the filtered object only; the test with `other.owner` pins that.
- Attempts to break it, none succeeded:
  - A field named only in a field-level grant (`permissions[0].objects.inv.fields.region`): key-as-reference under `WRITE_KEYS` records `carrier`; verdict `carrier-only`. Pinned by test.
  - A field named `using` or `check` on the object: a map key is read as a field only when the parent key is in `PREDICATE_KEYS` or `WRITE_KEYS`, and neither `rowLevelSecurity` nor `defaultRowScope` is. Inside a grant, `fields.using.when` ends in (`using`, `when`), so the last-two test is false. Not credited.
  - A field grant's `when`, a policy's `name` / `label` / `positions`: last segment is not a predicate clause; carrier.
  - The predicate text under another object key (`description`): no credit. Pinned by test.
  - Name-keyed `permissions` map: the set's name is one more leading segment; the last two are unchanged. Pinned by test.
  - `PERMISSION_SET_KEY_ALIASES` (`rls`, `policies`) and `RLS_POLICY_ALIASES` (`where`, `filter`): these feed strict-object refusals, not accepted spellings, so no accepted policy escapes the test.
- The `satisfies` typing is the right carrier for the key names: `PermissionSet`, `RowLevelSecurityPolicy`, `DefaultRowScope` and `ServiceObject` are all on the published api-surface. Whether it compiles is the in-progress `Type Check` runs' answer, not mine.
- Inline-grid credit, scope. Two call sites. (1) `walkObject`, inside the existing guard `field.inlineEdit` truthy, type `lookup` or `master_detail`, reference resolved: the same condition that already credits the join key, and the one `attachInlineSubforms` (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/providers/MetadataProvider.tsx` lines 714-715) uses to build the grid. (2) `walk`, for a `collection` child entry (`subforms` / `details`) only. A child that is not shown as an inline grid gets no credit: a relationship without `inlineEdit` is the pinned baseline (both sort-named fields reported); a `record:line_items` panel is a `panel` entry and is skipped; a page slot `details` holding components has no `childObject`; the parent's own sort-named field is not credited (pinned). Only the first sort-named field in child field order is credited; the second stays reported (pinned). "On every inline grid" in the PR body means every grid that is drawn, which is what the order asked for.
- The credit calls the spec helper with `{ fields }` from `fieldMapByObject`, built in declaration order whatever shape `fields` was authored in. It does not restate the list. Matches the card.
- nit: a policy with `enabled: false` is credited as a read although the runtime skips it. Same treatment every other site gets (no site consults an enabled/active flag); quiet direction.
- nit: in a predicate, a string literal or a `current_user.x` tail that equals a field name on the policy's object credits that field (`status == 'published'` with a field `published`). The dev disclosed the `current_user.email` half. Same scan as a sharing-rule `condition`; quiet direction by the rule's stated design.

**`packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts` (implementing).**

- Matches the rule now. The consumer paragraph names the RLS predicate in both carriers (`rowLevelSecurity[].using` / `.check`, an object's `defaultRowScope`) and the line-position field; the carrier paragraph now says "a field-level permission grant", which is accurate since a permission set is no longer a carrier in all its parts. The `Roots scanned` line is untouched and still equals `CONSUMER_ROOTS` / `CARRIER_ROOTS`.
- nit: the consumer list is a list of readers ("a formula … that names it; a predicate … that filters by it") and the new item is a field ("the line-position field an inline grid stamps …"), so the sentence is not parallel, and it does not say which grids (a relationship with `inlineEdit`, a `subforms` / `details` entry). Readable as is.

**Remainder, checked because the seat asked:** `examples/app-showcase/test/author-time-advisories.test.ts` loses exactly 16 lines: the section comment, a blank line, and the two entries (`showcase_invoice` · `owner`, `showcase_invoice_line` · `position`). No other entry is touched.

Findings: 0 must-fix · 1 should-fix (the Clause-② line) · 5 nits.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-sbhcs8`
Reviewed-by: `fable contract-review sub-agent of session_01WGufzh7cM8EmUX4T2CBNHX`

**VERDICT: PASS**
